question: Will the NSE IPO be open for subscription at any point on September 17 or September 18, 2026 (IST)?

calls.reasoning: Resolution reduces to a single question: does the public bid window open on or before Fri 18 Sep? Reference class: Indian mainboard IPOs opening for subscription within ~14 calendar days of SEBI final observations (received 4 Sep) — historically uncommon, ~20-25%. Adjust up substantially on question-specific evidence: Reuters sources put book-building at 11 Sep, price band ~15 Sep and listing in the week of 21 Sep, and under mandatory T+3 listing a listing by 25 Sep mechanically requires an open by 18 Sep; ET and Hindi press independently name an ~18 Sep open with ~25 Sep listing; Pitru Paksha from 26 Sep gives a soft reason to finish by 25 Sep. Adjust back down because: the RHP is still unfiled and NSE/SEBI pages read TBA as of 7 Sep; a 15 Sep band leaves only the bare two-working-day statutory minimum before an 18 Sep open, whereas comparable large issues (NSDL, Swiggy, HDB) used 3 working days, which lands on 21 Sep; and the entire IPO-tracker ecosystem converges on 21-23 Sep. All error in IPO scheduling is one-directional here — any slip of even one working day crosses the 19-20 Sep weekend and resolves NO — so the asymmetry argues for staying below the reported-target scenario's face value.

CALENDAR / DECIDING-BODY SCHEDULE (found, verified)
- Sept 2026 Indian equity-market holidays: Mon 14 Sep (Ganesh Chaturthi) is the only trading holiday; weekends 5-6, 12-13, 19-20, 26-27 Sep. Working days therefore: 7,8,9,10,11 | 15,16,17,18 | 21,22,23,24,25.
- 17 and 18 Sep are both normal working days (Thu, Fri). 19-20 Sep is a weekend, so a one-working-day slip past 18 Sep jumps to 21 Sep.
- Pitru Paksha 2026 runs 26 Sep (Purnima Shradh) / 27 Sep to 10 Oct; Indian issuers and bankers often, though not always, avoid launching or listing in this fortnight. Navratri begins ~11 Oct.
- Searched for an NSE/SEBI-published public-issue advertisement or RoC RHP filing date: none found as of 7 Sep — searched, absent.

REGULATORY MECHANICS (the arithmetic that binds the dates)
- SEBI ICDR: for a book-built IPO the price band must be disclosed at least TWO WORKING DAYS before bid opening. Therefore: band on 11 Sep -> earliest open 17 Sep; band on 15 Sep -> earliest open 18 Sep; band on 16 Sep -> earliest open 21 Sep; band on 17 Sep -> earliest open 22 Sep.
- SEBI T+3 listing (mandatory since Dec 2023): listing occurs on the 3rd working day after the issue closes. So close 18 Sep -> list 23 Sep; close 21 Sep -> list 24 Sep; close 22 Sep -> list 25 Sep; close 23 Sep -> list 28 Sep. A listing inside the week of 21-25 Sep requires a close on or before 22 Sep, which with the 3-working-day minimum bid window requires an open on or before 18 Sep.
- Minimum public bid window is 3 working days; anchor allocation is 1 working day before the public open (17 Sep anchor -> 18 Sep open).

Range 2-4 working days, modal 2-3. Source: contemporaneous Business Standard IPO reports.
- Conditional class: anonymous-source press reports naming a target IPO launch/listing week ~2 weeks in advance. No published hit-rate dataset was located; searched, absent.

calls.reconciliation: Disputes and checks (5 targeted retrievals, results including the empty ones): (1) Searched for an NSE price-band announcement / RHP-with-RoC filing / public-issue advertisement dated 5-7 Sep — NONE found; all live aggregator pages still show band, lot size and issue size blank. (2) Fetched ipowatch.in/nse-ipo/ directly (Chittorgarh and Business Standard 403 for the runs): it carries Open 21 Sep / Close 23 Sep / Allot 24 Sep / List 28 Sep, every date explicitly marked '(Tentative)', price band rendered as the unfilled placeholder Rs [.] to Rs [.], and an inactive RHP link. That settles Run 1's open factual question about the unverified X post claiming dates were 'DECLARED': they are not declared, and the tracker window is an auto-generated placeholder, not broker-sourced. It is also self-inconsistent with the wire reporting, since its 28 Sep listing falls outside the 'week of 21 September' every outlet attributes to NSE. (3) Confirmed via search that Reuters' reported plan is book-building from 11 Sep, band ~15 Sep, listing in the week beginning 21 Sep, with NDTV Profit relaying a band 'by September 11'; the 11-vs-15 Sep band split across outlets appears to be Indian outlets converting Reuters' 11 Sep book-building start into a band date. (4) Arithmetic check, settled FACTUAL: with 14 Sep the only holiday, T+3 gives close 22 Sep -> list 25 but close 23 Sep -> list 28; with a 3-working-day minimum book, any listing inside the week of 21 Sep requires an open on or before 18 Sep. Reuters' target and the tracker window cannot both be right. (5) Price-band lead time, settled FACTUAL and against all three runs' stated version: Hyundai Motor India advertised its band Fri 11 Oct 2024 and opened Tue 15 Oct 2024, i.e. opening on the second working day after the advertisement satisfies the requirement. So bands on 11, 15 or 16 Sep each permit a 17 or 18 Sep open; only a band on 17 Sep or later mechanically forces NO. The YES region is wider than Runs 1-2 assumed. Market check: no Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi or bookmaker contract on NSE IPO timing — none found, no anchor to blend. Remaining pure-JUDGMENT tie: whether to weight the observation-to-open base rate (Runs 1-2) or the reported-plan-holds base rate (Run 3). I break it toward the latter for branch selection, because the observation-gap class discounts a 21 Sep open nearly as much as an 18 Sep one and so cannot arbitrate between them; it belongs on the 'slips out of September entirely' branch, which I price at roughly 0.13. Landing at 0.48 — above the two low runs because their central discount is misapplied and their price-band arithmetic was too strict, below Run 3 because with zero official steps completed the one-directional slip risk into the 19-20 Sep weekend cliff is the modal failure and cannot be priced at 27%.
